summary: Built and filed the real-cluster witness for the stale-configuration consequence. The new harness grows an actual five-node in-memory cluster (bootstrap {A,B,C}, election, three committed applies, a user snapshot on A at index 6, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E) with the configuration entry committed at index 8, A shut down, {A,C} cut from {B,D,E}, A restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs from its own stores) and every node runs with the feature enabled so the restart reads the commit index the running protocol staged. Local construction feedback showed it discriminating as predicted: A's stored commit index is 8 and covers the configuration entry, the restarted A reports {A,B,C} instead of {A,B,C,D,E}, A becomes leader in the two-voter partition while C (current configuration, same partition) never does, B leads the three-voter partition, leader_count is 2, and both leaders commit different entries at index 11 in term 3, so the filed comparisons assert at most one leader, no same-index/same-term conflicting commits, no minority commit, and the current membership on the other side. A first local variant also exposed a necessary premise, now recorded as the @commit_index_staging behavior: tryStageCommitIndex returns immediately unless the node itself runs with RestoreCommittedLogs, so a deployment that never enabled the feature has stored commit index 0 and no divergence. The parent question's interpretation was corrected accordingly: the restart-shaped state is no longer merely supplied, since this experiment produces it through normal operations, and the election consequence is now its own filed experiment whose receipt is pending. Incomplete: that receipt and its comparison interpretation, the healing behaviour of two conflicting leaders, and the earlier registered question about constructor replay backpressure.
